sentences.text: Sneathia are described as urogenital anaerobes, with two species identified, Sneathia vaginalis and Sneathia sanguinegens.

The genus has been linked to bacterial vaginosis, preterm birth, chorioamnionitis, urethritis and HPV-mediated cervical carcinogenesis, although knowledge of its pathogenicity is limited by fastidious growth.
Sneathia vaginalis is described as a common component of the vaginal microbiome and is emerging as a marker for preterm birth.
It produces cytopathogenic toxin A, reported to be capable of lysing human red blood cells and permeabilizing epithelial cells.
In a 3D organotypic model of the human cervix, strains of both Sneathia species robustly induced IL-6 and IL-8/CXCL8 and triggered a conserved immune-mediated response.
